title: Semistable Galois alteration over a complete trait
statement:
A trait is $\operatorname{Spec}R$ for a Noetherian local domain of dimension one with principal maximal ideal. It is complete strictly henselian if $R$ is complete for that ideal, is henselian (simple roots of monic polynomials over its residue field lift), and has separably closed residue field. Its canonical log structure is $\mathcal O\cap j_*\mathcal O_\eta^\times$, where $j$ includes its generic point. Mixed characteristic means fraction-field characteristic zero and positive residue characteristic.

Let $S$ be a complete strictly henselian mixed-characteristic trait, and let $X$ be an integral regular scheme flat and quasi-projective of finite type over $S$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Quasi-projective over a scheme $B$ means admitting a locally closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^n_B$; projective means a closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^n_B$ followed by projection [def-kun-projective]. There exist a finite group $G$, a finite dominant trait extension $S^{\prime}\to S$ with $S^{\prime}$ complete strictly henselian, and an integral regular scheme $X^{\prime}$ quasi-projective of finite type over $S^{\prime}$ and over $S$, with a $G$-equivariant commutative square $X^{\prime}\to X$, $S^{\prime}\to S$. The action on $X,S$ is trivial, $a:X^{\prime}\to X$ is projective dominant, and there is a nonempty open $U\subset X$ on which $a^{-1}U\to U$ is a connected finite etale $G$-torsor [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. The scheme $X^{\prime}$ has semistable reduction over $S^{\prime}$: etale locally it has charts etale over $\operatorname{Spec}R^{\prime}[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(t_1\cdots t_r-\pi)$, where $1\le r\le n$ and $\pi$ is a uniformizer. Its divisorial fs log structure, trivial on the generic fibre, is $G$-stable, log regular [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and log smooth over the canonical log trait $S^{\prime}$ [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. No restriction on the degree $\#G$ is asserted. Finite means affine with module-finite coordinate algebras [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: Expose XVI 3.7, first two paragraphs and first sentence after the four bullets, p.254: normalization of constants followed by the semistable G-alteration (Vidal 2004b, Proposition 4.4.1). Geometric input only.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-normal-projective-compactification] to $X/S$. Obtain $S_0\to S$ and the normal integral projective $S_0$-scheme $C$, flat with geometrically integral generic fibre, with $X$ a dense open of $C$ and $k(C)=k(X)$. This is a change of the base through algebraic constants inside $k(X)$, not an alteration of $X$. It is essential that the ultimate generic cover be Galois over $k(X)$; composing an arbitrary constant-field extension with an alteration would not justify that assertion.

source.place: XVI 3.7, first paragraph and start of second paragraph, p.254

proof.text: Suppose first that $\dim C_{\eta_0}=0$. The projective generic fibre is proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper] and [lem-pc-projective-base-change], so [lem-pc-dim-zero-finite-over-field] makes this zero-dimensional integral fibre a finite field spectrum. Its geometric integrality forces this field to be $k(S_0)$ (a nontrivial finite characteristic-zero extension splits after algebraic closure). Thus $C\to S_0$ has finite generic fibre and is projective birational. It is in fact an isomorphism: the identity on the generic point extends to $s:S_0\to C$ by the valuative criterion [lemma-nagata-proper-valuative-criterion-existence-api], and $s\circ f=1_C$ since the two maps agree generically and the equalizer is closed in integral reduced $C$; similarly $f\circ s=1$. Here separatedness follows from properness [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper]. Then $X$ is a nonempty open in the trait $S_0$; take $X'=X$, $S'=S_0$, $G=1$, and $a=1_X$. The semistable chart is $\operatorname{Spec}R_0[t]/(t-\pi_0)\cong S_0$ restricted to this open. The log-structure verification is Step 7 below.

source.place: X 2.5 proof, omitted dimension-zero case; XVI 3.7 p.254

proof.text: For $d=\dim C_{\eta_0}>0$ apply [lem-per-trait-marked-nodal-alteration] to $C/S_0$. All its hypotheses are Step 1's conclusions. Write its output $q:Y_d\to C$ over $S'\to S_0$, with the finite group $G$ and marked split nodal tower. Keep the nonempty open $V\subset C$ where $q^{-1}V\to V$ is a connected finite etale $G$-torsor. The group acts trivially on $C,S_0$ and hence on $X,S$, but may act nontrivially on $S'$. No log smoothness or regularity of this nodal tower is being assumed.

source.place: X 2.5 proof, first application of Vidal 4.4.3, p.153; XVI 3.7 p.254

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-marked-nodal-tower-semistable-modification] to this same marked split tower with its $G$-action. It supplies an integral regular projective $S'$-scheme $Z$ and a $G$-equivariant projective birational $h:Z\to Y_d$, with the stated strictly semistable charts. Its splitting hypotheses are precisely those provided in Step 3. This step modifies the nodal tower; it does not use the later Sylow quotient or the prime-to-$\ell$ alteration that cites the present item.

source.place: X 2.5 proof, successive Vidal 4.4.4 modifications and remark, p.153

proof.text: The composite $q h:Z\to C$ is projective by [lem-trf-h-projective-composition]. Restrict it by the open immersion $X\hookrightarrow C$, putting $X'=Z\times_C X$. By [lem-pc-projective-base-change] the map $a:X'\to X$ is projective. It is dominant since $q h$ is dominant and $X$ is dense open. The source is a nonempty open of the integral regular $Z$, hence integral regular; regularity and the semistable charts restrict to opens directly. For the generic torsor choose a dense isomorphism open $O\subset Y_d$ for $h$, intersect all its finitely many $G$-translates, and set $F=Y_d\setminus O$. Properness of $q$ follows from [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper]; its closed-image property [def-weil-proper-morphism] makes $q(F)$ closed. It misses the generic point of $C$: its fibre there is the single generic point of integral $Y_d$, since $q$ is generically finite and the generic torsor is integral. Thus $U=X\cap V\setminus q(F)$ is nonempty open. Above $U$ the modification is an equivariant isomorphism, so $a^{-1}U\to U$ is the original connected finite etale $G$-torsor. Restriction to a nonempty open of an integral scheme preserves integrality, hence connectedness.

source.place: XVI 3.7, four bullets p.254; elementary restriction and removal of a proper closed image

proof.text: The composite $S'\to S_0\to S$ is finite directly from [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]: write the traits as spectra of $R\to R_0\to R'$. If $b_i$ generate $R_0$ as an $R$-module and $c_j$ generate $R'$ as an $R_0$-module, then the finitely many $b_ic_j$ generate $R'$ over $R$. It is dominant; $S'$ is already complete strictly henselian by Step 3. To check quasi-projectivity over $S$, apply [lem-fin-finite-over-projective] to the finite scheme $S'\to S$ and the identity projective $S\to S$: since $S$ is affine Noetherian it gives a finite-dimensional projective embedding of $S'$ over $S$. The projective composition theorem [lem-trf-h-projective-composition] makes $Z$ projective over $S$ as well as over $S'$. The open $X'\subset Z$ is therefore quasi-projective over both bases. Projective maps are finite type by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper] and the definition of properness [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The open $X'$ is quasi-compact because $Z$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; thus it remains finite type over either base by the affine-generator definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: XVI 3.7 p.254, projectivity and finite trait extension

proof.text: Give $X'$ the divisorial structure $M=\mathcal O_{X'}\cap j_*\mathcal O_{X'_{\eta'}}^\times$. On a semistable chart with $t_1\cdots t_r=\pi'$, use the log chart $\mathbf N^r\to\mathcal O$, $e_i\mapsto t_i$, and the base chart $\mathbf N\to R'$, $1\mapsto\pi'$. The compatible monoid map sends $1$ to $(1,\ldots,1)$. It is injective and its group cokernel is $\mathbf Z^{r-1}$: subtract the first coordinate from the others to exhibit the quotient. The comparison scheme is $B_r=\operatorname{Spec}R'[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(t_1\cdots t_r-\pi')$, and the semistable model is $\mathbf A^{n-r}_{B_r}$. The comparison map is the etale chart map, smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres], followed by the projection, smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]; it is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. $\mathbf N\to R'$ charts the canonical structure as $R'\cap K'^\times=\pi'^{\mathbf N}R'^\times$. Hence the fs chart definition [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale] gives log smoothness. The canonical log trait is log regular directly from [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]: at the closed point the nonunit ideal is $(\pi')$, the quotient is a field and $1=0+\operatorname{rank}\mathbf Z$; at the generic point the log structure is trivial and the field is regular. Apply [lem-trf-log-smooth-log-regular] with these injective torsion-free charts. It gives log regularity and identifies the local chart structures with the divisorial structure, so they glue to $M$. Its triviality locus is exactly the generic fibre, since inverting the product makes every $t_i$ a unit. The $G$-action preserves that fibre (automorphisms of the trait fix its closed point), so it preserves the subsheaf $M$. This verifies all log clauses also in the dimension-zero case, using $r=n=1$.
